messages.subject: Integrated habitat and species occurrence dynamics models
parts:
Hello unmarked community:

I am investigating occupancy patterns of a vole species that occupies discrete habitat patches and presents a metapopulation-like dynamics. I have occupancy data on four consecutive sampling seasons of over 600 habitat patches. The problem is that the habitat patches are highly dynamic between seasons, with some of them merging and separating over time, changing dimensions, and most importantly changing from suitable habitat patches to unsuitable to suitable again in subsequent seasons.

My question is if unmarked has integrated habitat and species occurrence dynamics models that could be used to analyze my type of data.

(MacKenzie, D. I., Bailey, L. L., Hines, J. E., & Nichols, J. D. (2011). An integrated model of habitat and species occurrence dynamics. Methods in Ecology and Evolution, 2(6), 612-622.)


Thanks in advance for any help/guidance

Helena

messages.author: 00ebeb6e0521112d
messages.subject: AW: [unmarked] Integrated habitat and species occurrence dynamics models
parts:
Dear Helena,

 

Unfortunately, unmarked does not have this. Since Jim Hines is an author of that paper you mention, I am quite certain that the model is incorporated into his PRESENCE software, so I would use PRESENCE. (I am not sure whether MARK has that model, may want to check.)

 

As I remember, their model is a version of a multistate model. These can of course be implemented in BUGS software as well, and this then confers the usual advantages of ease of extension in virtually any direction: e.g., random effects, “integrated models” (combining data sets with different protocols), ...…

 

Best regards  -- Marc
